title: B200 bring-up checklist (runtime hardware tuning profiles)
content:
Context
- Goal: validate B200 is safe to run in Redwood runtime and ship an initial tuned profile behind an experimental flag.
- Non-goal: perfect tuning on day 1. We need “safe defaults + measurable uplift vs baseline + fast rollback.”
- Owner(s): Isabella (microbench + SKU tuning), Hiro/Grace/Yuki (kernels/heuristics), Irene/Vanessa (fleet + rollout), Sean/Aisha (SRE + canary gates).

Scope for B200 bring-up (this checklist)
1) Software stack readiness (driver/CUDA/NCCL/container base)
2) Hardware detection correctness (SKU strings, multi-GPU, MIG/partitioning)
3) Microbench sanity checks (correctness + basic throughput/latency)
4) Perf suite runs on workload matrix (end-to-end)
5) Gating rules (feature flag + pool allowlist + canary thresholds)
6) Rollback plan + operator playbook (fast disable)


0) Pre-flight: confirm we’re testing the right thing
[ ] Confirm the runtime branch / release target (Connor O’Brien + release train notes)
    - runtime version:
    - profile pack version:
    - is this a backport candidate or mainline only?
[ ] Confirm B200 profile is gated behind experimental flag
    - Expected: profile selection should require BOTH:
      - GPU SKU detection == B200
      - feature flag enabled (e.g., runtime.profile.experimental_b200=true) OR explicit profile pin
    - Reference: PR-22021
[ ] Confirm fleet access constraints and which pools are available
    - pool(s):
    - region(s):
    - node counts (min for canary):
    - reservation window / timeboxing constraints:
[ ] Confirm success criteria for “bring-up complete” (minimum bar)
    - No correctness failures (token mismatches, NaNs, crashes)
    - No increase in error rate vs baseline (5xx, timeouts)
    - Perf within expected envelope for initial targets (see section 5)


1) Software stack versions (hard requirements + recording)
Record everything here so we can reproduce issues later.

1.1 Driver / CUDA / NCCL
[ ] NVIDIA driver version on host (nvidia-smi)
    - driver:
    - confirm matches the minimum required by B200 fleet image
[ ] CUDA version in container/runtime
    - cuda:
    - cudnn (if applicable):
[ ] NCCL version
    - nccl:
    - if multi-GPU nodes are in scope, confirm topology-specific settings are known/approved
[ ] GPU firmware / VBIOS (if we can access) noted in run artifact

1.2 Container + runtime build
[ ] Container base image tag recorded
[ ] Runtime build SHA recorded
[ ] Compiler/toolchain versions recorded (if custom build)
[ ] Ensure the runtime logs print: runtime version + profile pack version + compatibility matrix
    - Reference: PR-22041 (startup logs)

1.3 Kernel selection prerequisites
[ ] Confirm compiled kernels support B200 target arch
[ ] Confirm any “arch-specific” toggles are guarded (don’t assume H100 behavior)
[ ] Confirm quantization paths we support are at least smoke-tested (fp16/bf16; int8 if enabled)

Notes / gotchas
- If we see unexplained perf cliffs, first suspect mismatch between container CUDA and host driver.
- If NCCL errors appear, immediately de-scope multi-GPU tests until Infra confirms topology + versions.


2) Hardware detection + config selection correctness
This is mostly to avoid accidental “B200 runs H100 profile” or vice versa.

2.1 GPU SKU string normalization
[ ] Collect raw GPU name strings from all B200 nodes across providers
    - attach list to run artifact (or paste here)
[ ] Confirm normalization maps these variants to canonical "B200"
    - Reference: detection logic PR-21991 + Slack thread on SKU variants
[ ] Confirm ambiguous detection path is safe (falls back to generic profile, not experimental)

2.2 MIG / partitions / multi-GPU
[ ] Determine whether B200 nodes are partitioned (MIG/other)
[ ] Confirm policy:
    - If MIG present: do we treat each device independently, or disallow experimental profile?
    - Current recommendation (bring-up): DISALLOW experimental B200 profile when MIG/partition detected unless explicitly pinned.
[ ] If multi-GPU nodes used:
    - Confirm profile selection is per-process/per-device and consistent across visible devices
    - Confirm collectives settings are default-safe (no tuning) for bring-up

2.3 Observability hooks for oncall
[ ] Confirm metrics exist:
    - selected_profile_name
    - selected_profile_version
    - override_source (fleet default vs helm/customer pin vs env)
    - key knob values exported (at least scheduler mode + kv-cache budget)
    - Reference: PR-22027
[ ] Confirm debug endpoint / CLI exists to dump effective config
    - If available: run once on a canary node and attach output


3) Microbench sanity checks (fast signal)
Run these BEFORE full perf suite to catch obvious correctness/perf issues.

3.1 Correctness (must-pass)
[ ] Single request decode correctness smoke test
    - small model, deterministic seed
    - compare outputs vs known-good H100 run (within tolerance; exact match may not hold)
[ ] Stress test for numerical stability
    - long-ish prefill + decode
    - look for NaNs/infs in logs / CUDA errors
[ ] Load/unload + repeated init
    - start/stop runtime 10x
    - watch for memory leak / driver init errors

3.2 Basic performance (sanity, not optimization)
[ ] Prefill microbench across seq-len buckets (e.g., 256/1k/4k/8k)
[ ] Decode microbench at small and medium batch sizes
[ ] Measure:
    - tokens/sec (prefill + decode separately)
    - p50 latency
    - GPU utilization
    - HBM usage
[ ] Compare vs baseline B200 “generic” profile; if tuned profile worse by >5–10% across most buckets, do not proceed to broader rollout

3.3 Memory safety checks
[ ] KV-cache allocation behavior with long contexts
    - verify we respect kv-cache budget limits
    - verify runtime produces clear log when budget reached (not silent OOM)
[ ] Fragmentation smoke test
    - repeated variable-length requests for ~10–20 minutes
    - watch for memory growth / allocator warnings

Artifacts to save
- microbench command lines
- raw outputs
- runtime logs
- nvidia-smi snapshots


4) End-to-end perf suite (workload matrix)
Bring-up requires at least a minimal subset of the matrix; full matrix is for later.

4.1 Minimum workload set (bring-up bar)
[ ] 2 model families (one chat-style, one instruct-style) from current catalog
[ ] Sequence length mix:
    - short (<=512)
    - medium (~2k)
    - long (~8k) if memory allows
[ ] Concurrency levels:
    - low (1–4)
    - medium (16–32)
[ ] Streaming on for at least one workload (to catch scheduler/flush behavior)

4.2 What to record
[ ] p50/p95 latency (prefill vs decode if we have breakdown)
[ ] tokens/sec (aggregate + per GPU)
[ ] error rate, timeouts, retries
[ ] GPU mem peak + steady-state
[ ] tail latency stability over time (look for periodic spikes)

4.3 “Stop the line” criteria
[ ] Any correctness failure (NaNs, CUDA illegal access, frequent kernel launch failures)
[ ] p95 latency regression >10% vs baseline generic profile for the same workload (unless explicitly accepted as trade-off)
[ ] Error rate increase >0.2% absolute (or any customer-visible errors in canary)
[ ] Any OOMs in the minimum workload set


5) Gating and rollout plan (must be boring and reversible)
B200 should ship as experimental first.

5.1 Feature flag requirements
[ ] Default OFF globally
[ ] Enable only for:
    - internal perf suite jobs
    - allowlisted canary pool(s)
    - explicit per-deployment pin (Dedicated/Private) with “unsupported/experimental” label
[ ] Confirm oncall can flip OFF per pool/region without redeploy (Infra toggle / config push)

5.2 Canary phases
Phase 0: internal-only
[ ] One node, one region, synthetic traffic + perf suite

Phase 1: fleet canary
[ ] <=5% of B200 pool in one region
[ ] Duration: at least 2 hours of steady traffic (or equivalent load test)
[ ] Watch dashboards: latency (p50/p95), errors, GPU mem, queue depth, scheduler drops

Phase 2: expanded canary
[ ] 25% of B200 pool in region A
[ ] Optional: add region B if region A is clean

Phase 3: “available but gated”
[ ] Expose as selectable profile in internal tooling, still OFF by default

5.3 Canary gates (initial suggested thresholds)
These are starting points; Aisha/Allison can adjust once we see noise level.
[ ] p95 latency: no worse than +8% vs baseline generic profile on matched workload
[ ] tokens/sec: not worse than -5% vs baseline; target uplift +5–15% on decode-heavy workloads if tuning is doing anything
[ ] error rate: no worse than +0.1% absolute
[ ] OOM count: 0 (any OOM fails gate)
[ ] queue drops / backpressure: no worse than baseline


6) Rollback plan (explicit, rehearsed)
We need a one-page “how to stop the bleeding” procedure.

6.1 Rollback triggers (examples)
[ ] Any sustained p95 regression >10% for 15 minutes
[ ] Any increase in 5xx/timeouts correlated with profile enablement
[ ] Any OOMs after enablement
[ ] Any kernel crash / GPU reset events correlated with enablement

6.2 Rollback actions (in order)
[ ] Disable experimental B200 flag for affected pool/region
[ ] Force selection to generic profile (or previous known-good profile version)
[ ] If still bad: reduce concurrency / tighten queue limits (temporary safety mode)
[ ] If still bad: drain nodes and roll back runtime build (if suspected runtime regression, not profile)

6.3 Communications checklist
[ ] Post in #eng-runtime + #eng-sre with:
    - timeline
    - what was disabled
    - impact
    - dashboard links
[ ] If customer-facing impact: route to Support with a short summary + mitigation

6.4 After-action items (required)
[ ] Create/Update known-issues entry with repro + mitigation
[ ] Add/adjust perf-canary gate to catch this class of regression earlier
[ ] Tag any required code fix PRs and assign owners


7) Final “bring-up complete” sign-off
Required sign-offs before we call initial B200 bring-up complete:
[ ] Kernels lead (Hiro Tanaka): correctness + kernel compatibility
[ ] Scheduling lead (Sofia Ivanova or delegate): no obvious scheduler pathologies
[ ] Infra sponsor (Irene Choi): fleet readiness + rollback mechanism verified
[ ] SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher / Neha Kapoor org): canary gates + dashboards acceptable

Deliverables to attach when signing off
[ ] One consolidated benchmark summary (before/after)
[ ] Known limitations + maturity statement (“experimental”) for B200 profile
[ ] Link to runbook section for B200 rollout + rollback


Open questions / TODOs (as of last edit)
- Do we forbid experimental B200 profile when multi-GPU is detected (until NCCL tuning is validated)? Current leaning: yes.
- Minimum required driver/CUDA version: waiting on confirmed fleet image details from Infra + partner call notes.
- Which workloads best represent likely early B200 customers (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)? Need Applied ML input for realism.

Change log
- 2025-11-12: initial draft from bring-up sync notes
- 2025-11-26: added explicit canary thresholds + stop-the-line criteria
- 2025-12-08: added detection/MIG policy recommendation + observability requirements
